title: Fletcher as bandleader and businessman
summary: Roy discusses Fletcher's lack of business sense, recording deals for Moe Gale, Horace's role, and hard keys.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Let me ask you something about Fletcher. It's sometimes said that he was not a strong leader and that he was not a good businessman, and he sort of let the band go to pieces under him. Did he take care of business while you were with him?

Well, how do you mean that, did he take care of business? A lot of things happened that shouldn't have happened; I'll just put it to you like this. For instance, like, if it had been me, Benny Goodman wouldn't be broadcasting the same book I got. You understand what I mean?
He made some deals for recordings that I wouldn't have made. In fact, I didn't want to make them,

but I was the only one and I turned out to be the rebel, and everybody was looking at me with the fisheye, so I had to go along with it. For Moe Gale, you know. It was ridiculous, the prices they wanted us to record for, you know.

I know what you mean, because he was recording for Victor and so was Benny, and Benny had all those good arrangements. Well, some of the things Fletcher did were good, too, but some of those things he should have recorded, I guess. But then he did all that stuff with Benny in '35, and then he didn't have a band for a while, and I guess he did it for the money...

He did it right back there. That's what we used to get mad about. Here we come on, and right behind us here comes Benny with the same thing, you know. Don't forget, he didn't spend as much time rehearsing the band as Benny did, you know. I mean, Horace was the guy that took care of business, worked the band in shape. If he'd had more authority(?)... I really dug Horace.

But it's just one of those things, man. It was kind of... That era that that band come under, they were more or less a sportin' band, they had big cars and fur coats, and they were all like all-star instrumentalists and played in the worst keys...
Why did Fletcher write in those hard keys?
He said it's more brilliant there. But you know what it is, if you play those hard keys enough, you can play them...
